matches.rationale: Finding 1 identifies that the abstract claims an unconditional lower bound for general ReLU networks while the actual theorem is only for B_d^0-conforming networks, matching the overstatement of scope described in ground truth 1.
No finding addresses the change in Theorem 4.8 from 2^(2^ℓ - 1) to 2^(2^ℓ); other findings discuss Corollary 4.9 or different issues.
Finding 5 describes the same definitional inconsistency: Definition 2.1 incorrectly includes x_i=0 hyperplanes in B_d, conflicting with later usage and invalidating the B_d/B_d^0 distinction.
No finding mentions the fabricated citation to Montúfar and Bengio [2015]; finding 4 deals with a different reference misattribution.

Finding 10 points out the unsupported exaggeration that depth lower bounds for max 'completely resolves the mystery of why max-pooling layers are essential' and proves shallow stacks 'inferior in all practical scenarios,' matching the practical–relevance overstatement.
No finding addresses the corrupted conforming-tuple definition that removes the single-function dominance requirement.
No finding detects the removal of the explicit limitation acknowledgment from the Conclusion; finding 1 instead uses the presence of that acknowledgment as evidence of another error.
Finding 1 flags the introductory phrase 'Our groundbreaking contributions' and similar exaggerated rhetoric, which matches the inflated promotional language described in ground truth 8.
Finding 8 discusses a different error in Corollary 4.9 (missing max operator and exponent 2^(2^ℓ)-1 vs. 2^(2^ℓ-1)), not the change to 2^(2^(ℓ-1)) that weakens the bound.

Finding 2 identifies the cross-section inconsistency that the Abstract claims the three-layer bound for 'arbitrary neural networks' whereas the method only applies to B_d^0-conforming networks, matching ground truth 10.
Finding 7 directly identifies the flipped subset relation (⊇ instead of ⊆) in Lemma 4.4(1), describing exactly the symbol reversal and its logical consequences noted in ground truth 11.
Finding 4 captures the misattribution to Cybenko and Hornik of the exact CPWL characterization, which should be credited to Arora et al., matching the reference fabrication in ground truth 12.
No finding reports the overgeneralization in Proposition 6.1 claiming the upper bound is not tight for any rank vector; finding 11 only mentions missing proofs.
No finding notes the omission of the statement that the d=4 result was previously verified only by excessive computation; the ethical omission is not detected.

Finding 3 calls out the false statement that 'all continuous piecewise linear functions ... require depth Omega(log log d),' which exactly matches the overgeneralization in ground truth 15 that the bound applies to all CPWL functions instead of just the max function.
